CweFindings.Name: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition
CweFindings.Description: The product does not properly check inputs that are used for loop conditions, potentially leading to a denial of service or other consequences because of excessive looping.
CweFindings.Explanation: uploadPhotos iterates over every client-supplied multipart file at HomeController:69 and performs per-file image inspection/database work. The configured app.file-upload.max-files-per-upload=10 is never bound or checked. Thus attacker-supplied file count controls repeated expensive work with no application count limit. Authentication and the 50MB aggregate multipart size constrain exposure; this is a potential resource-exhaustion pattern, not an infinite loop.

CweFindings.Name: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value
CweFindings.Description: The product allocates memory based on an untrusted, large size value, but it does not ensure that the size is within expected limits, allowing arbitrary amounts of memory to be allocated.
CweFindings.Explanation: Anonymous GET / calls getAllPhotos, whose unpaged native query selects every row including photo_data. Photo.photoData is a byte[] @Lob with no lazy fetch configuration; all stored image bytes are materialized into the List on each gallery request although the template only needs metadata. Total allocated memory scales with the cumulative uploaded photo corpus without a result/aggregate-byte bound; individual 10MB file and 50MB request limits do not bound accumulated database contents. Repeated public gallery requests can exhaust heap once enough photos exist.

CweFindings.Name: Insufficient Logging
CweFindings.Description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.
CweFindings.Explanation: SecurityConfig uses the default HTTP Basic authentication entry point with no failure/access-denied audit handler or AuthenticationFailure event listener, and the repository has no authentication-audit listener or access-log configuration. Authentication failures occur before controller/service logging. Upload/delete success logs contain filenames/IDs but omit the authenticated principal, preventing actor attribution for destructive actions. Static assessment confirms missing application audit instrumentation; external proxy/SIEM logging was not available for verification.

CweFindings.Name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
CweFindings.Description: The product allows the upload or transfer of dangerous file types that are automatically processed within its environment.
CweFindings.Explanation: Authenticated uploadPhoto trusts client-supplied Content-Type at PhotoServiceImpl:87. ImageIO failing to identify a reader does not reject the file (124-143), and non-IO parser failures explicitly continue (149-152); arbitrary non-image bytes with an allowed image MIME are saved at 155-166 and subsequently served by PhotoFileController:75-83. This confirms content-validation bypass; no server-side execution or browser script execution was demonstrated.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
CweFindings.Description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.
CweFindings.Explanation: createPhotoCard interpolates user-controlled originalFileName into HTML text and quoted attributes at upload.js:185-189, then displayNewPhotos inserts the string using insertAdjacentHTML at 157. showErrors also writes file names into innerHTML at 216-218. HomeController returns those names from upload metadata at 78 and 87. Crafted filenames can inject elements/event handlers in the uploading user's origin. Upload is authenticated; this does not demonstrate anonymous cross-user stored XSS, and server-rendered Thymeleaf pages escape their text.
